messages:
alex: Heads-up — we had multiple cross-tenant evictions from the dedicated-gpu-eu pool this morning. Scheduler moved pods to hosted-gpu-1 and broke some network policies. Need a quick plan.

maria: Which namespaces and what errors from the scheduler/CA?

alex: Affected namespaces: tenant-a, tenant-b. Scheduler logs show `FailedScheduling: 0/10 nodes are available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu`. CA then spun up hosted nodes and pods landed there (no dedicated affinity).

jin: That sounds like either missing nodeAffinity or missing taints/tolerations on dedicated pools. If pods lack a hard affinity to dedicated nodes, CA will launch any available pool.

sam: We currently rely on a namespace annotation `gpu.pool=dedicated-<team>` plus a validations webhook that only checks format. It doesn't inject affinity or toleration.

lisa: Short proposal: 1) enforce required nodeAffinity in PodSpec (mutating webhook injects when `gpu.pool` set), 2) put a taint `dedicated-gpu=true:NoSchedule` on dedicated pools and have the webhook inject the matching toleration only for pods from that tenant.

maria: For autoscaler, we should label nodegroups `pool=dedicated|hosted` and prefer scaling dedicated first. CA has `expander=priority`/`least-waste` options — need config but CA can't enforce per-namespace rules itself.

jin: Right. CA chooses nodegroups but doesn't know tenant intent. The webhook + taint approach will stop accidental scheduling to hosted.

alex: Cost/network note: hosted nodes are preemptible and in a different VPC; when tenant pods drifted there we saw increased egress and intermittent policy drops. That caused customer errors. Also billing gets messy if workloads spill.

ops-bot: alert: cluster-autoscaler scaled up hosted-gpu-1 by 3 nodes at 2027-06-12T03:12Z (reason: pending pods: 12)

sam: We need chargeback tagging — annotate pods with `billing/tenant` and ensure our cost pipeline reads node labels so we can attribute costs when spill happens.

lisa: Timeline idea: hotfix this week = tighten webhook to inject nodeAffinity + required toleration; mid-term = admission + scheduler plugin to reject pods that try to schedule to wrong pool; long-term = operator to reconcile pool quotas per tenant and emit alerts.

maria: Agreed. Adding taint `dedicated-gpu=true:NoSchedule` on dedicated pools plus webhook-injected tolerations per-tenant should stop future spills.

jin: Note: expander `least-waste` will pack better but if tolerations missing it won't help. Webhook is step 1. I'll help run integration tests in staging dedicated pool.

sam: I'll open the PR to the webhook repo today — will add unit tests and an integration job that runs against the staging cluster. Also will add a metric `scheduler/evictions_by_cause` and a Grafana panel to alert on cross-pool evictions.

alex: Good. Can we also add an alert when CA scales hosted because dedicated pool is at 100% GPU utilization? That would make spills visible immediately.

maria: Yes — we can emit a recording rule `dedicated_gpu_utilization_ratio` and alert if >0.95 for 3m and hosted scales within that window.

sam: I'll wire that into pager duty as a low-sev for infra-first responders.

lisa: One gotcha: mutating webhook must be careful for older CRs and batch jobs. We'll only inject for pods with `gpu.pool` set. Fallback behavior documented.

alex: Timeline check — hotfix this week (webhook inject + taint), PRs by EOD, staging test early next week. Who owns the hotfix?

maria: I can do the webhook changes tomorrow morning. Sam owns the PR and tests. Jin helps staging. Lisa can review security/edge cases.

alex: :thumbsup: Thanks team, let's avoid another customer-facing spill.
